chain.title: A simple workshop power source
chain.desc: Feed the Coal Generator with supported solid fuel and connect a consumer or buffer. Begin with a small working circuit before adding advanced generators.

chain.title: A component for energy storage
chain.desc: Craft a basic Power Core for the first Powercell. It is an ingredient, not a generator; plan where the stored energy will come from.

chain.title: Buffer a machine's energy supply
chain.desc: Build a Powercell and configure its sides with the supported wrench. Test charging and discharging before joining it to a larger storage arrangement.

chain.title: Prepare a larger storage tier
chain.desc: Upgrade the Power Core using the installed recipe. Higher storage capacity helps with demand peaks but does not increase generation.

chain.title: Grow the local power buffer
chain.desc: Upgrade or build the next Powercell tier and configure its faces. Check the stored energy and network connections after changing an existing setup.

chain.title: Components for the largest local cells
chain.desc: Make the advanced Power Core when the workshop needs the larger storage tier. Build it for a measured energy requirement rather than as a prerequisite for every power system.

chain.title: Finish the local storage ladder
chain.desc: Install the higher-capacity Powercell and verify transfer under load. The other generator and remote-storage branches remain independent of this full upgrade ladder.

chain.title: Begin a remote-energy network
chain.desc: Place a Simple Dimensional Cell and configure its power sides. Prepare matching link cards before expecting separate cells to share energy.

chain.title: Link the intended cells
chain.desc: Initialize a Powercell Card and copy the intended link to the other cells. Verify the network identity before connecting a distant machine.

chain.title: Expand the dimensional-cell branch
chain.desc: Upgrade to the larger Dimensional Cell and preserve the intended link. Test remote energy transfer and account for the installed version's transfer behavior.

chain.title: A larger remote reserve
chain.desc: Add an Advanced Dimensional Cell when the linked network needs its capacity. Keep the supplying generator and consuming machines within practical transfer limits.

chain.title: A timing-based power project
chain.desc: Plan an Endergenic Generator loop with more than one generator and a Pearl Injector. Good timing produces energy; an idle generator is not a passive source.

chain.title: Start the pearl cycle
chain.desc: Place and configure a Pearl Injector for the generator loop. Supply pearls and deliberate redstone timing, then verify that pearls are received and relaunched correctly.

chain.title: Observe the timing state
chain.desc: Use an Ender Monitor to inspect generator state and support the control circuit. Tune the loop on a small setup before relying on it for the whole base.

chain.title: Prepare an alternative blaze-fuel route
chain.desc: Power a Blazing Agitator and supply blaze rods. Follow its rod-quality workflow before sending the output to the corresponding generator.

chain.title: Collect a prepared blazing rod
chain.desc: Produce a Blazing Rod and inspect its quality. Keep useful rods in the processing arrangement where the manual recommends rather than treating all rods as identical fuel.

chain.title: Use the prepared blaze fuel
chain.desc: Supply a Blazing Generator with prepared rods and connect the output. This is an alternative advanced power branch, independent of the Endergenic timing system.

chain.title: Read production and demand
chain.desc: Install a Power Monitor on the intended circuit and inspect its readings. Use observed consumption to decide whether the next upgrade should be generation, storage, or transport.

coverage.scope: Authored branched progression; item and component acquisition objectives, not automatic proof that a factory works.
limits: Creative cells are excluded. Endergenic timing and blazing-rod optimization are explained at milestone level, not supplied as a complete automation design.
Pack scripts, recipe changes, and other Minecraft versions require the installed-pack scan; this guide is not a complete mod manual.
coverage.verification: Local JAR item models and English registry names; selected recipes and bundled manuals checked. Not a new in-game playthrough.

notes: Re-reviewed 2026-10-07 against local Minecraft 1.20.1 JAR item assets and selected recipes/manuals, with official project sources listed separately. Every authored row now has explicit prerequisites; empty lists identify intentional branch roots. The coverage section states the verified versions and remaining limits. This replaces older list-order and item-count claims.
